title: A Lantern for the Regiment
premise: In the winter of 1917, Noor Zhou keeps the light at Gullwrack Point, believing the war and its storms belong to a world far away. When an unconscious child is left at their door with a note reading 'forget this face,' Noor recognizes the boy as kin to the family they abandoned twenty years ago to live under a borrowed name. As the great storms sever supply lines and a deserter arrives seeking shelter, Noor must decide whether to protect the child's secret, expose it for passage on the last ferry before the armistice — or surrender their own hard-won berth. In the end, Noor gives up the seat, keeps the child, and finally signs their true name in the lighthouse log, choosing memory over invisibility.
about_author: Ansel Underhill is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse keepers' logs along the northern coast. Their fiction is drawn from the marginalia keepers left between official entries.

chapters.title: The Log of Small Hours
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Establishes the rhythm of the light, the storms gathering offshore, and Noor's creed that history happens elsewhere. Emotional beat: quiet, controlled loneliness that reads as contentment but isn't.

chapters.title: A Parcel of Weather
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. During the first great storm, Noor finds a half-drowned child at the door with a note: 'forget this face.' The boy's features unsettle something old. Beat: dread disguised as practicality.

chapters.title: What the Sea Returns
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, with the child (Tam) semi-conscious. Noor nurses him, lying to themselves that he'll be handed to authorities when the weather lifts. Beat: reluctant tenderness cracking routine.

chapters.title: The Name I Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Noor's POV, 1897. The family betrayal — how Noor took a new name after a brother's crime and fled to the coast. Beat: shame revealed as the engine of identity.

chapters.title: Forget This Face
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor deciphers the note's handwriting: it belongs to their sister, Wren — meaning Tam is family, and someone knows where Noor hides. Beat: paranoia arriving like fog.

chapters.title: The Man Who Walked Out of the War
chapters.summary: Deserter Callum Frazer's POV. He stumbles into the station seeking shelter, carrying papers that could hang him. He notices the child. Beat: wary mutual recognition of two people hiding.

chapters.title: Rations and Rumors
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Noor and Callum. Supply boat fails to come; the three form an uneasy household. Radio reports hint the armistice may come by spring. Beat: domesticity as fragile truce.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, inland. She left the child deliberately, hunted by men her husband's debts brought to the door. Her letter explains why Noor specifically. Beat: love expressed as abandonment.

chapters.title: The Ferry Manifest
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A government notice: one final civilian ferry before winter closes the coast; berths require documented identity. Noor realizes documents mean names — and exposure. Beat: hope sharpened into dilemma.

chapters.title: What Tam Remembers
chapters.summary: Tam's POV, age nine. He remembers his mother's instructions and begins testing whether Noor can be trusted, offering fragments of the family story Noor fled. Beat: the past speaking through a child.

chapters.title: Callum's Bargain
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. He offers to forge papers in exchange for silence about the child — he needs a berth too. Three claimants, two seats. Beat: complicity tightening like a knot.

chapters.title: The Storm Between Us
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The worst storm of the year; the lamp mechanism fails mid-passage and Callum saves the light at cost of his injured hands. Beat: trust built in crisis, complicating betrayal.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor writes to Wren for the first time in twenty years, then burns the letter. Interleaved: Wren's unsent replies found later. Beat: grief for time that cannot be recovered.

chapters.title: The Inspector Comes Ashore
chapters.summary: Inspector Hale's POV. A naval inspector arrives investigating deserters and undocumented persons, drawn by the failed supply runs. He interviews Noor. Beat: the outside world finally knocking.

chapters.title: Two Berths, Three Names
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor drafts false papers giving berths to Tam and Callum, leaving none for themselves — then discovers Callum has secretly done the reverse. Beat: sacrifice meeting sacrifice.

chapters.title: What Hale Knows
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Hale has matched the child's description to a missing-persons circular and suspects Noor's identity too. He offers a trade: the boy for Noor's cooperation. Beat: power corrupting duty.

chapters.title: The Long Night Watch
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor keeps the light through a night of decisions, revisiting every escape they ever made. Tam sits with them, asking who he really is. Beat: the truth offered honestly for the first time.

chapters.title: Armistice Eve
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. News of the armistice reaches the coast; bells ring across the water while the ferry loads at dawn. Hale waits at the dock. Beat: celebration as pressure cooker.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Climax, Noor's POV. At the gangway, Noor puts Tam aboard with papers in Callum's name, exposes their own true identity to Hale to draw scrutiny away, and stays behind as the ferry pulls out. Beat: renunciation as victory.

chapters.title: After the Bells
chapters.summary: Callum's POV, at sea with Tam. The boy asks if Noor will be punished or forgotten. Callum, pardoned under armistice terms, chooses to testify for Noor. Beat: loyalty repaid at distance.

chapters.title: The True Name
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Hale, moved or pragmatic, records Noor's statement but files no charges; the war's end dissolves the case. Noor writes their birth name in the log for the first time. Beat: identity reclaimed, quietly.

chapters.title: A Lantern Lit for Two
chapters.summary: Resolution, Noor's POV, spring. Wren arrives on the first supply boat, hollowed but alive; Tam returns by summer. The three keep the light together through calm seasons. Final beat: memory chosen over forgetting, home redefined.
